01 · Where I can help

My view of what business needs today

Four challenges I have taken on before, and I am ready for new ones.

  1. A clear picture of how the business really runs

    I map how work, people, data and money connect, and then redesign the parts that slow everyone down.

    At Silpo, store managers could see the part of their store's P&L they control by the 5th of the following month.

  2. A next-generation project office

    I built and led a project office at Silpo and trained project managers. Today I build a new kind: a PMO that uses AI itself, launches AI projects, and works closely with IT teams that build with AI. After launch I write the results into standards, so the gains don't slide back.

    At Silpo, while the chain grew from about 120 to 300 stores: more than 20 legal entities merged into one, acquired chains integrated, a practical project management course for retail.

  3. AI with clear rules

    In my systems one AI proposes, a second AI from another vendor checks it, and a person decides. Scripts verify the numbers. Sensitive data goes out only with explicit consent. I would bring the same rules to your teams.

    That is how I built my car-audio tuning method: I gathered approaches, documentation, instructions, libraries, and my own and friends’ experience, and AI helped turn them into a system. In 2026 it brought me five competition awards and a first place to one of its users.

  4. Operations, commerce, finance and IT in one conversation

    I studied systems programming and worked as a CTO. I also studied business management and decision economics, served as an expert in a McKinsey operations working group, and at Silpo ran projects on promotions, pricing, markdowns and assortment. I can talk to operations, commercial teams, finance and IT without a translator.

    At Ciklum, as CTO, I planned and budgeted IT while the company grew from about 50 to 250 people. At Silpo the project office planned store headcount, payroll and productivity from planned revenue.

Now

Applied AI

I am one of two partners at FlipManager, a startup building an AI exoskeleton for managers: digital assistants that take routine off people and support them in their daily work. We are developing four products on one shared base:

  • DPA, a digital personal assistant for a person's projects and ongoing activities, at work and in life.
  • DBA, an assistant for a small business owner.
  • DPC, a personal assistant for managers inside a company.
  • DCC, Digital Company Compass, a compass for the company as a whole.

We are working from both ends. I build the assistants for individuals and for small business owners. My partner is working on security at enterprise level.

I am also designing PMO Hub: a toolkit that helps managers organise and coordinate projects, from a department up to a whole project office. I already run my own work with it. PMO Hub started as a tool for managing the development of DPA, and later both of my car-audio projects were built with it.

That is where I find out what works before I recommend it to anyone. The car-audio tuning method needed all of my experience: electronics, software, project discipline and, now, AI.

What I have built with AI

A personal assistant, a project office, car-audio tuning projects and this website itself. In each, several AI models have separate roles, agents and tests do their part, but a person always makes the final call.

Private · FlipManager

Digital Personal Assistant (DPA)

Ask for a demo ↓

DPA is an exoskeleton assistant for everyday tasks, email, and project planning and tracking, at work and in life. Each area, project or initiative has its own space, and a shared dashboard shows the big picture and highlights what matters. The assistant remembers where things stand, transcribes meetings, records tasks and agreements, draws conclusions, and asks a second AI for an independent opinion. No sensitive data goes to an outside model without anonymisation and my explicit "yes".

Public · 2 repositories

Autosound: Tuning Skill and TCC

Skill on GitHub ↗ TCC on GitHub ↗

One project in two parts for tuning car audio built around a sound processor. I gathered the approaches, documentation, instructions, libraries and experience (mine and friends’), and with AI's help built the skill on that base: it makes the overall process deterministic while keeping AI flexible at every step. The skill follows a seven-phase algorithm, from intake to final listening, and works through many interacting factors at once: the car's acoustics, every speaker, crossovers, time delays, phase and equalisation. Real measurements and maths lead it to the best settings. The skill works in Claude, Codex and Antigravity.

TCC is a full desktop application built on top of the skill: multilingual, for macOS and Windows, with live measurements, the predicted result, the tuning plan and an AI chat panel. It works together with the skill and can use different AI models, directly or through the OMP tool.

In both, Claude calculates and proposes settings, a model from another vendor checks, critiques and corrects them, and the person listens and decides. Nothing changes the processor by itself.

7phases in one fixed tuning process
14major and minor releases of the skill since June 2026
4,300+automated tests in TCC
4languages; macOS and Windows

Results in 2026: my own car won five awards at EMMA and AYA championships, including two first places in qualifying rounds and third at the German EMMA Final. One user's car took first place at the AYA Finale.

04 · First steps

How I see the first 100 days

AI can bring quick results, but how far they go depends on which data the company’s security rules allow AI to work with. So I start by assessing these constraints. Finding how to use AI under strict security rules can be a task of its own.

  1. Goals and directionUnderstand where the company is going: its goals, priorities and the direction of change.
  2. Pains and quick winsFind the most pressing problems and the places where the largest gains can come quickly, so the start pays off.
  3. Team, plan, deliveryForm the team, set goals, draw up plans, then coordinate and implement. With AI each step goes much faster than usual.
  4. Scaling AIHow AI is scaled depends on the company’s goals and how it sees the role of AI. It can mean building new solutions, helping each person in their daily work, or a company-wide system that connects people’s knowledge and work.
